blue_whale.in_the_wild: All oceans, mostly offshore; migrates between polar feeding and tropical breeding waters.
blue_whale.caveats: Never kept in human care; no pilot institution relevant. Museum skeletons are the only 'see it' option.

giant_squid.in_the_wild: Deep ocean worldwide, rarely seen alive.
giant_squid.caveats: Not kept alive anywhere; only preserved specimens at natural-history museums (out of scope for this batch).

narwhal.in_the_wild: Arctic waters around Canada, Greenland and Russia.

emperor_penguin.caveats: Almost never kept (SeaWorld San Diego is the known exception); every pilot match is 'related' via other penguins.

albatross.in_the_wild: Southern Ocean and North Pacific open seas.

african_elephant.caveats: Pilot sites hold Asian elephants (related) except Wildlife Safari, whose page does not name the elephant species; left out.

parrot.caveats: Generic entry: macaws, rosellas and parakeets counted as exact per rule 7. Consider whether the finder should de-duplicate parrot vs macaw vs cockatoo.

kangaroo.caveats: Generic 'Kangaroo' taken as exact for true kangaroos (red, western grey); wallabies, wallaroos and tree kangaroos recorded as related.

lemur.caveats: Generic entry; a few pages say 'lemurs' without species.

crocodile.in_the_wild: Tropical rivers and coasts of Africa, Asia, Australia and the Americas.
crocodile.caveats: Treated as generic for family Crocodylidae; gharials/Tomistoma and caimans excluded.

viper.caveats: Generic; rattlesnakes are pit vipers but were recorded only under 'rattlesnake' to avoid double listing.

grizzly_bear.in_the_wild: Western Canada, Alaska and the northern Rockies.
grizzly_bear.caveats: Pages that say 'brown bear' without subspecies are recorded as related.

method_notes: PILOT B, institution-centric. Wall clock about 20 min in total for 14 institutions: 4 min fixed overhead (AZA list, accreditor checks, one batched Wikidata/Commons call), then 0.5 to 2 min each. Fast: a server-rendered A-Z or paginated directory (Oregon Zoo 162 entries over 14 pages, Oregon Coast Aquarium 133 over 11 pages, Seattle Aquarium, Zoo Boise, Toronto Zoo region pages, Chester), all by curl plus a slug grep. Medium: sites that give curl a 403 (Cloudflare) but load in a real browser (Woodland Park, Point Defiance, NW Trek, Zoo Boise, AZA itself). There I fetched the exhibit or habitat pages from inside the page with same-origin fetch() and read the h2 to h5 names. Slow: JS-rendered pages (High Desert Museum returned an empty DOM through fetch, so I had to navigate and reject the cookie banner) and sites with no list at all (Wildlife Safari is a Shopify store with prose only, so its holdings come from the encounters, village and adopt pages; 2 are MED). USABLE LISTS: 13 of 14 (93%) had some structured list of animals on the institution's own site. 8 of 14 (57%) looked complete (Oregon Zoo, OCA, Seattle Aq, Zoo Boise, Toronto, NW Trek, Point Defiance, HDM ambassador page). 4 were curated subsets that under-count: Taronga Sydney shows only 28 featured animals, Zoo Berlin about 55 species or area pages, Chester 83 of its roughly 500 species, and Woodland Park's exhibit pages name only headline species. Idaho Falls Zoo is a City of Idaho Falls page (fact-sheet index), which may include past animals, so all its rows are MED. ACCREDITATION: AZA directory https://www.aza.org/find-a-zoo-or-aquarium (240 institutions as of March 2026; curl returns 403, the browser works). I filtered its text for 'Wash.', 'Ore.' and 'Idaho', which gave 10 institutions. High Desert Museum is AZA-accredited but is a museum with live animals, so it is recorded as type museum with AZA accreditation. Toronto Zoo is NOT on the current CAZA accredited list (caza.ca/accredited-institutions). It is AZA-accredited through March 2027, so it is recorded as AZA, not CAZA. BIAZA has a public list at biaza.org.uk/members/all (/members is a login wall). The ZAA list is at zooaquarium.org.au/public/Public/Find.aspx and shows Taronga Zoo Sydney as a Regional Member. EAZA's member map ships its full data in the Gatsby file https://www.eaza.net/page-data/membership/page-data.json: 451 members with name, membership type, country and lat/lng, of which 348 are zoos or aquariums. That covers DE about 48, FR about 55, ES about 20, GB about 55 and IE 5. It is the single best seed for the European part of the build. COORDS AND IMAGES: 13 of 14 have Wikidata P625. Idaho Falls Zoo (Q42309306) has no coordinates, so I took OSM way 957725462. 3 had no P18, so I took files from the Commons category. I rejected 'OCAq Entrance.jpg' because the uploader is the aquarium's own marketing account. Zoo Berlin's P18 is a giraffe photo taken in the zoo; a gate photo may be preferable. PROBLEMS: (1) Curated featured lists silently under-count, so absence from a list is never evidence of absence. (2) Cloudflare 403s on curl for about 40% of US sites, so a headless browser is required. (3) Generic app entries (parrot/macaw/cockatoo, kangaroo/red_kangaroo, anaconda/green_anaconda) create double rows; the finder UI should decide how to show them. (4) Name traps seen and skipped: 'Mantella (Poison Frog)' at Toronto is not a dart frog, Toronto's monocled cobra is not a king cobra relative worth pairing, and clouded leopard is not a leopard. (5) Pages rarely carry dates, so 'live in 2026' relies on the page being current. SCALING TO ABOUT 600 (AZA 240 + CAZA about 30 + BIAZA about 100 + EAZA DE/FR/ES about 125 + ZAA about 100): about 1.5 min of agent time per institution plus a 10 to 15% manual review, which comes to about 15 to 20 agent-hours, or 2 to 3 hours of wall clock with 8 parallel agents in batches of 10 to 15 institutions each. Per-site parsers are not worth writing. The pattern that worked was: find the list URL (usually /animals), pull every link slug or heading, then run a shared alias table (app id to common names, German, French and Spanish names and scientific names), with a human or LLM resolving generic and related cases. Build the alias table once, before scaling. Non-English sites (Berlin in this pilot) need the DE/FR/ES names. Expect about 10% of sites to have no list, like Wildlife Safari. Those need prose mining at MED confidence or should be skipped.
